extracted.intended_audience: authors and researchers reporting formal studies of quality improvement in healthcare
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and reporting formal studies of quality improvement in health care, centered on the SQUIRE checklist and an Explanation & Elaboration document that provides examples and analyses for each checklist item.

rubrics_metrics.name: SQUIRE checklist (19 items)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SQUIRE statement consists of a checklist of 19 items that authors need to consider when writing articles that describe formal studies of quality improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Explanation & Elaboration (E & E) document provides one or two published examples for each SQUIRE item, followed by analysis of how the example expresses the intent of the guideline item. The E & E is intended to assist authors in preparing manuscripts describing QI projects for publication; the full statement and supporting material are available at http://www.squire-statement.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt standard scientific reporting elements for QI context
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of the items in the checklist are common to all scientific reporting, but virtually all of them have been modified to reflect the unique nature of medical improvement work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying common reporting elements (e.g., background, methods, results, discussion), authors should modify their content and emphasis to capture features unique to improvement work such as context, iterative interventions, process measures, and practical implementation details. The E & E gives examples and analyses illustrating these adaptations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use statistical process control (SPC) charts and annotate interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Example of a statistical process control chart (g-chart) with notation of when intervention occurred (Figure 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present longitudinal process data using SPC methods where appropriate; annotate the chart to indicate timing of interventions and relevant control limits (e.g., UCL). Use SPC to demonstrate changes in process performance over time and to support claims about intervention effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a study flow diagram
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a study flow diagram to depict study processes or participant flow (Figure 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear diagrams showing steps in the study or improvement initiative, participant or unit flow, exclusions, and temporal sequencing of interventions to aid reader understanding of study design and execution.
